messages:
marta: Heads-up: staging deploy queued for 1.4.x. Small doc updates + a change that lowers default request timeout from 30s -> 20s when unset. Need to decide semver and tagging before prod window.

deploy-bot: @marta scheduled a deploy to staging at 10:45 UTC. CI: all checks passed.

jon: What's the exact change surface? Is this a bugfix or behavioral change?

marta: It's a behavioral default change — we expect fewer stuck requests, but some callers relying on 30s might timeout earlier. No API shape change.

sasha: If defaults change user-observable behavior, it's not a pure patch. I'd argue minor bump (1.5.0). :thinking:

tao: OTOH minor bumps propagate differently in ecosystem. For our downstreams, ^1.x semver means minor bumps can auto-upgrade them. That could surprise customers.

jon: Proposal: ship as patch (1.4.3) but gate the new default behind an env flag `REDWOOD_TIMEOUT_NEW_DEFAULT=true` for one release, add prominent release notes, and monitor. If we see >0.5% error delta rollback. Vote?

sasha: I'm worried about "hidden" behavior behind a flag; customers who don't set it still get old behavior but might later pick up the change. If we plan to flip later, we should call it out loudly. -1 to silent patch.

marta: Agree on loud communication. My suggestion: patch with opt-in flag for first rollout, add a follow-up minor bump later when we flip by default. Release note header: [Behavioral changes — default timeout].

jon: Tagging question: do we use metadata in git tag? e.g. `v1.4.3-behavior` vs plain `v1.4.3`? We usually keep tags simple so tooling like `git describe` and CI release matching stays predictable.

marta: Keep tag `v1.4.3` only. Put details in annotated tag message and changelog. We can add a release note tag: `[behavioral][flag-gated]`.

tao: Also remember package consumers: if we released 1.5.0 later, folks with `^1.4.0` would auto-upgrade. So timeline/communication matters. Recommend we mention "to avoid automatic minor upgrades, pin to ~1.4.x in the short term" in notes.

sasha: Ops checklist: pin base image digests, set image tags to the annotated tag, and include rollback steps. If we proceed as patch + flag, ensure the flag flipping is documented here.

marta: Decision for today: 1) Release as 1.4.3 (semver: patch) 2) Gate new default behind env var `REDWOOD_TIMEOUT_NEW_DEFAULT` 3) Add `Behavioral changes` entry in changelog + customer-facing note 4) 48h elevated monitoring and rollback threshold of 0.5% error increase. Everyone okay? React with +1 / -1.

jon: +1

sasha: -1 (only because I want the flag to be opt-out not hidden — but will OK the plan if we add a banner in the dashboard/announcements)

tao: +1

deploy-bot: Staging deploy completed at 10:47 UTC. Canary metrics look within baseline for 30m. Scheduled prod window opens at 23:00 UTC; will do 10% canary for 15m then ramp.

jon: On tagging mechanics: I'll create an annotated tag `v1.4.3` and include a message: "semver:patch;change:default-timeout;ff:REDWOOD_TIMEOUT_NEW_DEFAULT" so it's searchable.

marta: I'll draft the release note + customer banner and attach the rollback playbook link. Also adding the kube snippet for ops: `kubectl set env deployment/redwood REDWOOD_TIMEOUT_NEW_DEFAULT=false` and image rollback `kubectl set image deployment/redwood redwood=registry/repo:v1.4.2 --record`.

sasha: Add short instructions for customers to pin: `npm install package@~1.4.2` or `pip install "redwood==1.4.*"` in the notes.

deploy-bot: Prod canary started at 23:00 UTC (10%). Monitoring alert if error rate delta > 0.5%.

marta: Thanks all — I'll cut the tag and PR in the next 20m and post links here. If anything changes I'll @channel update.
